name: Question 3
problem: Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ${\int }_{C}y\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}s,$ where $C$ is the section of the curve $y=2{e}^{x}$ for $\,0\le x\le 2?$
worked_solution:
Notice that the given curve is of the form $y=y(x).$ Therefore, by setting $x=t,$ we have $y=y(t)=2{e}^{t}.$ This gives the following parametrization of the curve:

$$
r(t)=⟨t,2{e}^{t}⟩,\,0\le t\le 2
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{e}^{t})j \\  & =i+2{e}^{t}\,j \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(2{e}^{t})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+4{e}^{2t}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=y\operatorname{cos}⁡x$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =2{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{0}^{2}f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}2{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot \sqrt{1+4{e}^{2t}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\sqrt{1+4{e}^{2t}}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ∫Cycos⁡xds, where C is the section of the curve y=2ex for 0≤x≤2?

a
 2∫02etcos⁡t1+etdt
b
 ∫02etsin⁡t1+4e2tdt
c
2∫02etcos⁡t1+4e2tdt
d
 4∫02cos⁡t1+4e2tdt
e
 ∫02sin⁡t1+4e2tdt
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Notice that the given curve is of the form y=y(x). Therefore, by setting x=t, we have y=y(t)=2et. This gives the following parametrization of the curve:

r(t)=⟨t,2et⟩,0≤t≤2

Computing r′(t) and ‖r′(t)‖, we get the following:

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(t)i+ddt(2et)j=i+2etj‖r′(t)‖=(dxdt)2+(dydt)2=12+(2et)2=1+4e2t

Now, since f(x,y)=ycos⁡x, we obtain

f(r(t))=2etcos⁡t.

Therefore, we can write the integral as

∫Cf(x,y)ds=∫02f(r(t))‖r′(t)‖dt=∫022etcos⁡t⋅1+4e2tdt=2∫02etcos⁡t1+4e2tdt.
